findings.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 — [advisory, confidence 100, severity P2] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates once while this module is imported, so every later source serialized onto an outbound job reports the worker-start timestamp instead of its own enqueue time; although no current consumer reads it, retaining it as provenance makes the next consumer’s age/order decision wrong, and that counterargument does not survive because `queued` is explicitly carried through `to_dict()` rather than being omitted.

src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:441 — [P1, confidence 75] `sync_status_inbound_task.apply_async(kwargs={"integration_id": self.model.id, "organization_id": self.organization_id, "issue_key": issue_key, "data": data})` never carries the newly added `assignment_source`, so a status update received from an integration is re-exported to that same integration and the cross-system status-sync cycle remains unblocked.

src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 — [P2, confidence 100] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates once when this module imports, so every `AssignmentSource.from_integration` serializes the same stale queue timestamp instead of the time that individual cross-system sync was queued.

tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:215 — [P1][confidence:100] The cycle-prevention test injects `assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` directly into `GroupAssignee.objects.assign`, so it never exercises the changed inbound assignment/deassignment path or Celery dict round trip and passes when `sync_group_assignee_inbound` fails to propagate the source, causing the originating integration to receive the outbound update and re-enter the sync cycle.

goldens.comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.

Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.
to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:215 — [P1][confidence:100] The cycle-prevention test injects `assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` directly into `GroupAssignee.objects.assign`, so it never exercises the changed inbound assignment/deassignment path or Celery dict round trip and passes when `sync_group_assignee_inbound` fails to propagate the source, causing the originating integration to receive the outbound update and re-enter the sync cycle.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a test coverage gap. Looking at the diff, `sync_group_assignee_inbound` in `src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py` was modified to pass `assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` to `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign`. However, the test `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` directly calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` with the `assignment_source` parameter, bypassing the inbound sync path entirely. This means if `sync_group_assignee_inbound` failed to properly pass the `assignment_source` parameter, the test would still pass. The test doesn't verify the full integration path where an inbound assignment from an integration should not trigger an outbound sync back to the same integration. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for the cycle-prevention feature being added.
